correctness.rationale: Every self-inverse partial affine bijection preserves its affine domain. Writing its restriction as \(f(x)=(I+N)x+b\) forces \(N^2=0\) and \(Nb=0\); the image/kernel/quotient classification counts all square-zero N of rank r with no overcount. Exactly \(2^r\) translations yield \(2^{k-r}\) fixed points, while \(2^{k-r}-2^r\) are fixed-point-free. Gaussian affine-domain count gives all joint coefficients. Normalized finite-product weights and a proved q-binomial identity give the parity limits; dominated convergence over the summable Gaussian tails gives the codimension distribution, total asymptotic and global 1/2. The packaged verifier exhaustively checks actual GF2 maps and all predicted cells through d=4; finite tests alone do not prove the limit.

value.rationale: The domain-size versus number-of-fixed-inputs distribution is a canonical, complete structural invariant of self-inverse elements of the finite binary affine-partial inverse monoid, which models reversible partial affine computations. It proves genuine fixed-point gaps for all domain dimensions, plus a non-obvious limiting parity phenomenon (conditional limits \(1/2\) plus/minus \(0.06056\ldots\)) that exactly cancels to overall 1/2 via an explicit codimension distribution. This is an infinite-family structural and probabilistic classification, not an arbitrary enumeration slice or a restatement of existing linear involution counts.
